candidate.derivedAnswer: C: Some students are not fraternity members
candidate.answerReason: A student who is not honest exists by statement I. That same student cannot be a fraternity member, since statement II would then make the student honest.

methods.label: Follow one student guaranteed by statement I
methods.explanation:
Statement I guarantees at least one student who is not honest. Consider that same student. If the student were a fraternity member, statement II would require the student to be honest, contradicting the way the student was chosen. Therefore that student is not a fraternity member.

Hence some students are not fraternity members, choice C.
methods.levelReason: Only the ordinary meanings of “some” and “all,” together with a direct contradiction, are needed.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task requires tracking the same existentially guaranteed student through a universal restriction. This is precisely quantified logical inference. The meanings of universal and existential quantifiers are supporting knowledge; no set-operation representation is required by the written method.
